newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end up on rise in A index.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end up on rise in A index.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended up on Friday, encouraged by a solid rise on the A share market as investors shrugged off fears of possible official intervention to cool the markets down, brokers said.
The B index rose 0.796 points or 0.85 percent to 94.131 points on volume of 33.304 million shares worth $22.644 million, compared with $23.091 million on Thursday.
The A index surged 66.254 points or 4.51 percent to 1,534.115 points on turnover of 13.05 billion yuan after no solid measures to cool down the market were made public, brokers said.
Domestic institutions bought Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development following gains in the company's A shares, helping to push the B index up, brokers said.
Shanghai Lujiazui ended up $0.054 or 3.57 percent at $1.564 on volume of 2.7 million shares.
"There was bargain-hunting triggered by the gains in Lujiazui and the rise in the A shares," one broker said. "But many investors are still sidelined due to concerns over a clampdown."
"The movement of A share index will determine the direction of the B shares in the near future," another broker said.
Shanghai Worldbest was the star on institutional buying, surging $0.063 or 9.44 percent to $0.730 on volume of 1.4 million shares.
Market giant Shanghai Chlor Alkali Chemical was the most actively traded share on bargain-hunting late in the session, rising $0.002 or 0.54 percent to $0.366 on volume of 3.3 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index rebounded on active bargain-hunting during the afternoon session on bullish sentiment, brokers said.
The SSE30 blue chip index soared 188.088 points or 4.60 percent to 4,280.214 points.
Beijing Tianqiao Department was the best performer helped by institutional buying, surging 0.81 yuan or 10.06 percent to 8.86 yuan on volume of 5.6 million shares.
